labels.notes: Refuted at :521: ¬ ∀ (M : Type) [TopologicalSpace M] (C C' : Causality M) (V W : Opens M), V ≤ W → C.InextensibleNestedOn C' W → C.InextensibleNestedOn C' V. This is exactly the reading 'C, C' fixed, nesting on W and V ≤ W ⇒ nesting on V', the one the target's evidence and ladder.toml:854 ('not known to pass to a smaller open') ask about. Refuting it at Type 0 refutes it in every universe. It is not vacuous: a ¬∀ proved by an explicit witness, CoarsePoint with C = allRelated, C' = diag, V = nearOpens, W = ⊤. I checked the witness by hand. The topology's open sets are ∅, nearSet and univ. step is allRelated-inextensible in nearOpens (its image is all of nearOpens) and not diag-causal (it jumps at 0). The nesting holds on ⊤ only vacuously: Cantor gives a far point the curve misses, arctan squeezes the parameters below π/2 < 2, and the curve pauses at its last point and appends that far point at 2. The SCOPE discloses all of this: not T1, not T0, second countable but unproved, allRelated not causal, vacuous at M. The added conjunct ∀ W, AbsolutelyMinimalOn W for both causalities is the hereditary form of OQ-95. It gives the on-M form through Precausality.absolutelyMinimal_iff (Causal/Generated.lean:275), so 'either form of DEC-167's gluing' holds. In fact it is proved for every precausality on CoarsePoint. The sufficient condition mono_of_inextensible (:146) takes an explicit curve hypothesis hV, disclosed as not a ladder node. The T2, second countable refutation (the circle) is argued only, and disclosed as such. My check finds the argument sound, with a precision issue (finding 3).

findings.what: The argued T2 refutation names C as 'the cut line on the circle, which is causal' and describes it only by its curves. Transplanting Causal.cutLine's own convention (x ≤ y iff x = y, or x < y with y ≠ a; the relation may pass the cut point and may only not end at it) to ℝ/3ℤ gives a relation that is NOT causal: two distinct points other than p are related both ways around the circle. The argument is sound under another construction. ≤_U is a clockwise arc in U from x to y with p ∉ (x, y], plus x = y. ≪_U adds x ≠ p, so that I⁻ stays open at p. Under that construction C is causal and the rest checks: every C-inextensible curve of the circle starts at p and returns to it, so its image is the circle; in V = circle ∖ {q}, the arc from p to q is C-inextensible and C'-extensible behind p. The finding concerns an argued claim, not Lean, but the claim is stated as a fact and may reach the ladder.
findings.fix: Write out C's ≤ and ≪ in the docstring and the REPORT, as above. Say that C is not cutLine's convention transplanted.

findings.what: 'In both examples the curve of W that contains the V-curve covers, through W \ V, the points that C' adds inside V' does not describe the Lean example. On CoarsePoint no C-inextensible curve of W exists at all (the nesting holds vacuously), and diag adds no point: the step fails because it is not a diag-causal curve, not because C' extends it. The next sentence, 'When C' is causal (and the space Hausdorff), that route is closed; the case with C and C' both causal is the open one', is an unproved heuristic. It also leaves out the case C' causal, C not causal on a T2 space.
findings.fix: Confine the sentence to the circle example. Mark the 'route is closed' remark as heuristic, and state the open case as 'T2, second countable, C' causal' (or both causal), consistently with the question in REPORT.questions[0].
